snippet.title: Snickers overnight oats by @fitfuelbyjuliana #oats #overnightoats
snippet.description:
Recipe:
50g oat flour* (or oats blended to flour OR
regular oats)
30g of vegan vanilla protein powder* (important for thick texture!)
100g of Greek yoghurt or skyr 
5g milled flax seeds
10g peanut butter powder*
90ml of water or milk (1 just used water)
For the caramel layer:
5-10g of peanut butter + 5-10g of maple syrup mixed together
For the shell:
20g of dark chocolate*, and peanuts if desired

Mix together the ingredients for the oats and place into a ramekin/bowl. Refrigerate to let thicken for 1-2 hours..
Make the caramel then spread over the oats.
Melt the chocolate in the microwave and drizzle over the top to form a shell. Refrigerate overnight and enjoy!

snippet.title: [지식뉴스] ※긴급점검※ "사실 지금은 오히려 기회입니다"...'빚더미' 코어위브가 무너지면 AI도 끝날까? 윤쎈이 본 시장이 놓치고 있는 결정적 신호 / 교양이를 부탁해
snippet.description:
삼성전자와 SK하이닉스를 필두로 코스피가 흔들리고 있습니다. 'AI 부채' 공포에 코어위브가 폭락하고, 주말 내내 "이러다 다 무너지는 것 아니냐"는 불안이 번졌죠. 그런데 바로 그 급락의 한복판에 긴급 출연한 한 전문가는 정반대로 말합니다. "지금은 오히려 기회"라고요. 모두가 던질 때가, 오히려 남의 가치를 싸게 가져올 찬스라는 겁니다.

이 역발상을, 경제평론가이자 前 LS증권 리서치센터장 윤지호가 풀어냅니다. 윤 평론가는 지금의 하락을 '붕괴'가 아니라 '의심의 구간'으로 봅니다. AI가 미래를 바꾼다는 기대는 꺾이지도 않았는데, 사람들이 걱정거리를 새 이야기인 양 떠들며 '의심에 의심이 자가복제'되는 국면일 뿐이라는 거죠. 그래서 그는 "명품백을 갑자기 싸게 던질 때 받아내는 게 낫지 않냐"며, 지금 배당수익률이 가장 좋은 종목으로 삼성전자를 꼽습니다. 하방 위험보다 위로 열릴 리턴이 클 때 투자가 성립하는데, 8천·9천 포인트일 때가 아니라 바로 지금이 그 구간이라는 겁니다. 나아가 그는 시장이 왜 실적이 사상 최대인데도 주가를 안 올리는지를 설명합니다. 이제 시장은 '얼마 벌었나(이익)'가 아니라 '통장에 현금이 있나(ROIC·FCF)'를 묻기 시작했고, 그 잣대로 보면 삼성·하이닉스는 '너무 싸다'는 거죠. 하이퍼스케일러가 2028년에 흑자로 돌아서려면 메모리가 돈을 못 벌어야 하는데, 정작 메모리 회사 앞으로 엄청난 현금이 쌓여간다 그래서 "2028년을 지금 줍는다"는 것이 그의 결론입니다.

📌 윤지호 l 경제평론가 (前 LS증권 리서치센터장)

snippet.title: Leo Became a Superhero on Halloween... His Outfit Surprised Everyone! | Slow English (A2 Level)
snippet.description:
Maya Ate an Expired Pudding... Then She Had to Go to the Hospital! | Slow English (A2 Level)

What happens when you eat your favorite snack without checking its expiration date? Join Grace, Ethan, Maya, and Leo in this easy English story about expired food, stomach pain, a frightening family situation, and the importance of being honest when something goes wrong.

Grace decides to clean out the refrigerator, and Maya is excited to help her. While looking through the food, Maya discovers a chocolate pudding she has been missing for days. Unable to resist her favorite treat, she eats it without checking the expiration date and tries to keep it a secret from Grace.

Soon, Maya begins to feel pain in her stomach, but she doesn't want her family to know what happened. When Leo realizes that his sister is in serious discomfort, he quickly calls for help. Why is Maya feeling so sick? Will her family discover what she ate before her condition gets worse?

This episode of Grace Daily English uses slow, clear English and natural conversations to help A1–A2 learners improve listening comprehension and build practical vocabulary related to food safety, expiration dates, stomach pain, hospital visits, and describing symptoms.

---

✅ Slow and clear English conversations  
✅ Useful vocabulary about refrigerators, snacks, and food storage  
✅ English words for expiration dates and expired food  
✅ Everyday phrases for checking whether food is safe to eat  
✅ Vocabulary for chocolate pudding and other desserts  
✅ Natural expressions for describing stomach pain and discomfort  
✅ Useful phrases for explaining symptoms and feeling unwell

✅ Expressions for admitting a mistake and telling the truth  
✅ Useful phrases for apologizing and accepting responsibility  
✅ English for expressing worry and comforting a family member  
✅ Words for describing feelings: hungry, uncomfortable, worried, frightened, and relieved  
✅ Clear pronunciation through simple sentences  
✅ Speaking, shadowing, and listening comprehension practice  

---

✔️ Beginner English learners

✔️ Learners who want to improve speaking and shadowing  
✔️ Building everyday vocabulary about food safety and health  
✔️ Practicing English for describing symptoms and asking for help  
✔️ Anyone who wants to understand useful expressions for everyday emergencies  

Learn English naturally with Grace Daily English through simple stories, clear conversations, and practical everyday expressions. Improve your listening and speaking skills while learning about food safety, communicating when you feel unwell, and why it is important to tell someone when you need help.

snippet.title: 6 Hidden Cohorts Beat 7,000 Horsemen
snippet.description:
Battle of Pharsalus, 9 August 48 BC, in Thessaly, Greece: Julius Caesar's 22,000 foot faced Pompey's 45,000 foot and 7,000 horse. Pompey planned to ride his cavalry round Caesar's right wing and win from behind. Caesar pulled six cohorts out of his rear line and hid them behind that wing. When the horsemen swung round, the cohorts rose and drove their spears at the riders' faces, the cavalry fled, and Pompey's army broke behind them.

More from Pharsalus:
• The faces order is not in Caesar's own account. It comes from Plutarch, Appian and Florus. Caesar wrote only that the six cohorts charged and the horse fled, and that the victory must have its beginning from those six cohorts.
• Plutarch tells it as young nobles afraid of scars, but Caesar's own list of Pompey's horse is mostly foreign contingents plus slaves and herdsmen, so the tale is part truth and part colour.
• Caesar never gives the cohorts' headcount. Appian and Plutarch give 3,000, but Caesar's average cohort that day was 275 men, which makes six cohorts 1,650.
• Pompey rode out of his own camp in plain clothes and was killed in Egypt six to seven weeks later. Caesar pardoned the soldiers who surrendered.
• The 24,000 prisoners and 15,000 dead are Caesar's numbers, and Pollio, who fought there, put the Pompeian dead at 6,000.

Sources: Caesar, Civil War, book 3; Appian, Civil Wars, book 2; Plutarch, Life of Caesar and Life of Pompey; Frontinus, Stratagems; Florus, Epitome.
